reason: The copied instructions and amino acids appear to be the materials the repair cell needs to make collagen.
expectation: The cell will use the instructions and available amino acids to make a collagen protein.

effect: The repair cell used the RNA instructions and amino acids to make collagen chains; the chains now need processing and export.
reaction: The intact RNA template and growing chain make the protein-building step clear.
reason: The processing and export membranes are the available structures for preparing and delivering the new collagen.
expectation: The membranes will process the collagen and help export it from the repair cell.

effect: The cell processed and exported the collagen, producing supporting fibers that can now replace material in the wound. The membranes had to be used through the cell hotspot.
reaction: The automatic correction was helpful, though the required hotspot was not obvious from my first attempt.
reason: The new fibers appear to be the support material needed beneath the scrape.
expectation: The fibers will fill in the missing support beneath the damaged skin.

effect: The new fibers filled the deeper gap, while the surface cells still need to close over it.
reaction: The cross-section makes the distinction between deeper support and surface closure clear.
reason: The cells at the scrape’s edge are positioned to renew the missing surface.

choice.combine: Skin cells at the scrape’s edge

expectation: The edge cells will help close the surface gap, possibly with the available repair signals.

effect: The repair signals prompted edge cells to divide and spread; those cells now appear ready to close the remaining surface gap.
reaction: The sequence makes the signals’ role clear, though I had guessed they might be included automatically.
reason: The spreading cells should now be able to cover the gap in the rebuilding body.
expectation: The cells will close the surface gap and renew the protective skin layers.

effect: The surface gap has closed, while the deeper collagen is still remodeling; closure does not mean repair is finished.
reaction: The earlier-and-later comparison made that distinction clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making and exporting collagen was the most worthwhile passage: it connected protein production inside a cell to support outside it.

leastWorthwhile.text: The processing step was initially confusing because I expected the chains to combine directly with the membranes rather than through the repair cell hotspot.

surprise.text: The RNA template remained intact while amino acids were joined into a collagen chain.

arbitrary.text: Using the repair cell hotspot for processing was not obvious to me, although the resulting picture explained the cell's role.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: seeing the support and surface repaired separately, with deeper remodeling still underway, made me curious about what happens next.
